briefings.title: Gary Gensler Talks AI Competition with China | Bloomberg Talks
briefings.tldr: Former SEC Chairman Gary Gensler warns that the current AI investment boom is twice the scale of the 1990s internet bubble at 2.5% of the U.S. economy, posing serious revenue challenges for domestic market leaders like OpenAI and Anthropic due to cheaper Chinese models and private credit exposure.

briefings.title: There's Existential Risk Of AI Agents 'Not Aligning' with Their Humans, Says Gensler
briefings.tldr: Former SEC Chair Gary Gensler warns that the AI investment boom—double the relative size of the 1990s internet bubble—faces severe structural challenges from Chinese open-weight models, existential safety risks of misaligned AI agents, and systemic vulnerabilities in the retail-heavy private credit market.

briefings.title: Hester Peirce Explains What Crypto Still Needs Before She Leaves the SEC

people.name: Scott Melker
people.role: Host, The Wolf Of All Streets

briefings.tldr: SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce outlines how the agency is using existing authority to advance crypto regulation through a new five-year tokenized stock innovation exemption following the Clarity Act's failure.

briefings.title: Investing Starts with Education | Material Matters with SEC Chairman Paul Atkins

people.name: John Moses
people.role: Director of the Office of Investor Education and Assistance

briefings.tldr: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Chairman Paul Atkins and John Moses, Director of the Office of Investor Education and Assistance, discuss the critical importance of bottom-up financial education, highlighting the transformative rollout of tax-advantaged "Trump Accounts" for children and modern defense strategies against increasingly sophisticated AI and cryptocurrency scams.

briefings.title: Hester Peirce: The Positive Future of Digital Asset Regulation (Huge Catalysts Coming)
briefings.tldr: SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce highlights the agency's efforts to modernize market structures through the proposed removal of the 20-year-old Rule 611 and the upcoming "innovation exemption," emphasizing that future regulations must pragmatically support on-chain finance while fiercely protecting investor privacy, self-custody, and developer freedom.

briefings.title: Hester Peirce: The Positive Future of Digital Asset Regulation (Huge Catalysts Coming)
briefings.tldr: SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce highlights a pivotal shift toward digital asset integration, emphasizing the SEC’s proposed elimination of the 20-year-old Rule 611 and the development of an "innovation exemption" to facilitate controlled, on-chain financial experimentation.

briefings.title: SEC’s Hester Peirce: ‘We Lost Time’ on Crypto
briefings.tldr: SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce acknowledges that the U.S. "lost time" on crypto regulation due to an enforcement-first approach under previous leadership, but she expresses optimism that a new DC consensus—driven by both legislative efforts like the Clarity Act and SEC-led guidance—is finally providing the industry with the necessary regulatory framework.

briefings.title: Watch CNBC's full interview with SEC Chairman Paul Atkins
briefings.tldr: SEC Chairman Paul Atkins is shifting the agency away from "regulation by enforcement" toward a growth-oriented "ACT" strategy (Advance, Clarify, Transform) designed to lure innovative firms back to the U.S. and remove regulatory barriers to revitalize the public IPO market.

briefings.title: Commissioners Set the Course | Material Matters with SEC Chairman Paul Atkins
briefings.tldr: The SEC is pivoting back to its "core mandate" of disclosure-based regulation and capital formation, prioritizing the establishment of a clear, "fit for purpose" regulatory framework for digital assets to ensure the United States remains the global leader in financial innovation.

briefings.title: SEC Chair Paul Atkins and SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce in Conversation
briefings.tldr: The SEC is pivoting from "regulation by enforcement" to a collaborative, guidance-based framework, spearheaded by "Project Crypto"—a joint initiative with the CFTC—and a proposed "Innovation Exemption" to facilitate regulated experimentation in tokenized securities and DeFi.
